 Advertisement Updated: 6:36 PM CST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Sen. Chuck Grassley dismisses retirement claims
 Updated: 6:36 PM CST Nov 5, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ , Iowa — U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley has confirmed he will serve out the remainder of his eighth term, addressing speculation about a possible early resignation. 
 A spokesperson for Grassley posted on social media, saying, "He remains committed to delivering for the people of Iowa, who overwhelmingly elected him to a six-year term in 2022."
 Advertisement This content is imported from x. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site. Senator @ChuckGrassley is not resigning. He remains committed to delivering for the people of Iowa, who overwhelmingly elected him to a six-year term in 2022. #GrassleyWorks 
— Jen (@jeniowa2505) November 5, 2026 
 In September, Grassley told Republicans at a fundraiser, "I don't plan on dying in office," but added that he didn’t "want a Democratic governor choosing his replacement if he did." This comment raised questions about whether Grassley might retire early, allowing Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds to appoint his replacement before her term ends. 
 Grassley's office has confirmed he plans to serve out his current term. The senator has also filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission for the 2028 election, though he has not announced whether he will run again.
